title: If You Don't Understand How Banks Create Money, You Don't Understand Money
alts: Banks Don't Lend Your Savings. They Type New Money.
Where Does Your Money Go When You Put It in the Bank?
hook: When a bank gives someone a loan, it doesn't hand over anybody's savings. It creates new money, in the borrower's account, with a few keystrokes. That's not a conspiracy theory: it's what the Bank of England explained in 2014. Here's how it works, what limits it, and why it makes booms bigger and bank runs possible.
sources: Bank of England, 'Money creation in the modern economy', Quarterly Bulletin 2014 Q1 (McLeay, Radia, Thomas)
